meta.verdict_states_note: Condition states (met / with a change / not met / not applicable or declined / not yet known / not judged) describe single conditions only. There is no match verdict: decided 13 Oct 2026 — the tool lays out trade-offs by party and does not rank or score options. Wording is suggested for J.B. to accept.
meta.source_roles_note: source_roles (added 12 Oct 2026): for each source, the term of the formula it supplies, its role (coefficient · bound · proxy · check · site fact · rule · data · method · gap) and its own confidence on the register scale; verified=false marks a placement that is Claude's reading of the coefficient text rather than an explicit tie, for J.B. to confirm. A quantity's own confidence is not recomputed from these: it was set in verification and can sit below its sources where the transfer or an assumption is the weak link (status says why), or above a source used only as a check or bound. The md lists every quantity where own confidence differs from the lowest coefficient-role source, for review.
meta.calibration_note: Calibrated 13 Oct 2026 against built cases (sources/13_calibration_cases.md; calibrate.py; calibration_report.md): COP formula changed to full Lorenz with η 0.40–0.50; utilisation band widened to 0.20–0.60; heat_captured (E_reuse) added and ERF redefined to ISO/IEC 30134-6; heat_delivered renamed 'heat available' and the match quantity capped by receiver demand; two ownership models recorded (utility-owned free-heat; supplier-owned paid).

steps: build every combination the tool knows (size, position on the parcel or another parcel, adjacency, technology, both cities, in or out of town)
report the gates first — grid connection (r_grid) and zoning use (z_use): a blocked gate is named before any exchange is weighed, and the exchanges still show as "if the gate moved"
set aside options that break a user limit — and keep them for the "if you moved this limit" panel
drop options worse than another on every row for every party (not a trade-off)
compare positions in the building as options where the user has not fixed one (basement · ground · upper floor · roof), each with its floor load, fuel, flood, vibration and street-front rows
pick as many as the user asked for, as different as possible on the rows the user emphasised

let the user try things on any option — "what if we added…" — whether an opportunity for the place (a seasonal heat store, cooling for neighbours, batteries for the grid), something the place offers (reclaimed water, neighbours' greywater, the ground), or a technology choice (solar, water recovery, cleaner backup power) — and show what each changes and the rules in each city
show them side by side, in no order, each with its full trade-off table
run each option through the four futures (as planned · tenant changes cooling · tenant leaves · receiver leaves) and show what changes

quantities.coef: City of Vancouver: 333 wells in export; depth median 59 ft (p10 16, p90 210); static level median 11 ft; yield sparse (114 values, p90 100 USgpm); 2 open-loop geoexchange wells; Edmonton: AWWID (retrieval guide F6), not yet in hand
quantities.status: Vancouver in hand (government export); Edmonton pending AWWID

quantities.name: Cost of reserved (unused) capacity
quantities.formula: (capex + non-power opex) × (1 ÷ occupancy − 1); i.e. the share of a built-but-empty data centre that the offerable capacity carries
quantities.coef: Barroso §6.5: scale by inverse of occupancy; two-thirds full → +50% opex; half-full: server TCO $8,981 vs $6,310

quantities.name: BC Hydro long-run marginal cost
quantities.formula: value of energy or capacity a data centre frees up or avoids = LRMC × quantity; capacity value of flexible load = $300 + $110 per kW-yr of firm reduction at peak
quantities.coef: 2025 IRP App. F: energy $97/MWh (F2025$; UEC at POI $77 from the 2024 Call for Power levelized bid, + firm transmission 3, network upgrades 6, integration 8, losses 5, time-of-delivery −3); capacity $300/kW-yr point estimate (range 150–400); distribution and non-bulk transmission $110/kW-yr; dual-fuel dwellings cut Lower Mainland peak demand ~75% vs all-electric (Fig. 2-7)

quantities.name: What is seen from public space
quantities.formula: for each plant element: seen from public space / closed to view / known only from documents / not checked — tested the same way at every site
quantities.coef: J.B. field ledger per site (sources/12); permit record for the documented column
quantities.status: observation (J.B. to set the confidence level for 'seen on site'; proposed 80 for existence, no capacity)

source_roles.term: seen / closed to view / not checked

quantities.name: Surveillance as experienced
quantities.formula: visible cameras and signs; indicative watched area past the lot line (camera position and aim); first-person account labelled as one person's
quantities.coef: e.g. 55 E 7th: camera 'almost on the public edge' of the front door; 111 E 5th: dome under soffit, mast camera at roof corner, '24 hour video surveillance' signs in the lane (J.B., Oct 2026)
quantities.status: observation; never a guide to coverage gaps — only what a passer-by sees and how it feels

quantities.name: Sewer as heat source or sink
quantities.formula: Q = flow × 4.18 × ΔT, within the temperature rules: sewage arriving at the plant ≥ 11 °C when used as a source (KWL design rule); waste entering a facility < 40 °C, non-domestic waste < 65 °C when used as a sink (Bylaw 299)
quantities.coef: Vancouver: ~45 MW city-wide, ~100 MW region-wide (KWL 2014, secondary); NEU uses 3.2 + 6.6 MW; access first-come first-served with a letter of support (UT-008); heat user pays access costs; per-pipe flow near a parcel is not published (only North Surrey 6 MW). Edmonton: no EPCOR sewer-heat programme or data found; non-contact cooling water to sanitary sewer needs EWSI written approval (Bylaw 18100 s.5.10); Edmonton: Blatchford's planned sewer heat exchange centre (two combined sewers under the future market area) was deferred after EPCOR reduced its sewer-flow forecasts (Blatchford Budget and Plans 2023–2026) — the first Edmonton evidence on sewer heat, and a caution
quantities.status: rules in hand for Vancouver; flow at a parcel and all Edmonton figures are gaps

quantities.name: Sea or river water as a cooling sink
quantities.formula: capacity set by the thermal limit at the outfall and mixing, not by the licence: marine ±1 °C (BC, CCME), Burrard Inlet proposed "no further increase"; Alberta freshwater +3 °C over ambient
quantities.coef: BC licence: cooling application $1,000; heat-exchange rental $2.25 per 1,000 m³ (min $200); DFO intake screens 2.54 mm, approach velocity 0.035–0.055 m/s (internal conflict — confirm); Alberta Water Act review as for any industrial project; Toronto Enwave precedent: 4 °C in, ≤13 °C out, 50-year agreement
quantities.status: rules in hand; capacity is site-specific and unmodelled

quantities.name: Solar from roofs nearby
quantities.formula: roof area × kWh/kWp (NRCan municipal values) × kWp/m²
quantities.coef: NRCan municipal kWh/kWp values blocked — J.B. retrieval D9; a 0.1–40 MW load would use a roof's output on site

quantities.name: Rules for generation beside the data centre
quantities.formula: export cap and compensation by province; connection priority for paired generation (Alberta)
quantities.coef: BC: RS 2289 from 1 Jul 2026, export up to 100 kW per phase (or ≤100 kW nameplate) at $0.10/kWh, same or adjacent parcel; RS 2289 applies only at distribution voltage, so a data centre supplied at 60 kV or higher (RS 1830) cannot use it; community generation up to 2 MW. Alberta: micro-generation ≤5 MW (retail credit <150 kW, wholesale above); data centres paired with dedicated new generation or storage go to the front of the connection line (Alta Reg 117/2026, government summary)

quantities.name: Price of power at the site
quantities.formula: tariff for the customer class: BC Hydro LGS or Transmission (RS 1830); Alberta pool price + EPCOR (Edmonton) or FortisAlberta (Parkland) distribution and transmission
quantities.coef: BC LGS (RS 1600–1611, effective 1 Apr 2026): $13.83/kW, 6.79 ¢/kWh, 29.99 ¢/day; RS 1830 (supply at 60 kV or higher, effective 1 Apr 2026): $12.178/kVA, 4.914 ¢/kWh; loads >150 MW pay full incremental cost; 300 MW AI + 100 MW DC allocation. Alberta: pool $43.68/MWh (2025), $62.78 (2024); EPCOR DAS-TOUP and SAS-TOUP; FortisAlberta Rate 63; Rate of Last Resort not available to these loads. Replaces the first attempt's assumed $80–120/MWh

quantities.name: Water the place can supply
quantities.formula: potable at the metered rate; reclaimed where a utility offers it to industry
quantities.coef: Vancouver 2026: water $4.091–5.128 per unit + sewer $7.960 per unit (unit = 2.832 m³), no large-user rate; Metro Vancouver reclaimed water case-by-case, no rate. Edmonton: EPCOR supplied 4,226 ML of reclaimed water to industry in 2024 (price, customers not stated); commercial potable rates not extracted

quantities.name: Existing building to convert
quantities.formula: parcels with buildings whose use and age suit conversion (from the parcel tables), less what policy steers to other uses
quantities.coef: Precedents: 515 W Hastings office → Bulk Data Storage (2023); Edmonton office → data centre (2009, 2011), warehouse → data centre (Qu EDM2); Vancouver Downtown Office Conversion Policy addresses residential conversion only; no official vacancy statistics in either city
quantities.status: precedents in hand; stock at a parcel needs the parcel tables (N1–N7)

quantities.name: Acoustic cover from the place
quantities.formula: the zone pair sets what is allowed; a louder zone is the cover — Vancouver credits no ambient noise for equipment
quantities.coef: Vancouver By-law 6555: quiet→quiet 55/45, activity→quiet 60/55, intermediate or activity→other 70/65 (day/night); background credited only for commercial premises. AUC Rule 012 road categories credit ambient but apply only to power plants and substations. Neither city publishes a road-noise map (traffic counts only). Edmonton Bylaw 14600 limits pending (J.B. retrieval D1)
quantities.status: Vancouver in hand; Edmonton to recheck

quantities.name: Closeness to networks and customers
quantities.formula: distance to the nearest interconnection point and to customers; latency targets of tens of milliseconds
quantities.coef: Why operators locate in cities: third-party (colocation) firms favour urban settings for buyer proximity (Pan Fang & Greenstein 2025); backbone networks are biased to cities that serve as interconnection points (Malecki 2002); edge latency targets of a few tens of ms, VR under 16 ms (Satyanarayanan 2017); internet exchange and customer proximity (JLARC 2024). Locations of internet exchange points in Vancouver and Edmonton not yet sourced
quantities.status: rationale sourced; local exchange-point locations a gap

quantities.name: Zoning: allowed, conditional or rezoning
quantities.formula: look up the district: outright / conditional (development permit) / not listed (rezoning or text amendment)
quantities.coef: Vancouver: "Bulk Data Storage" (s. 2) is conditional in I-2, I-1C, I-3 sub-area A and FC-2 only; not permitted elsewhere, including all commercial and mixed-use districts; CD-1 site-specific. Edmonton: no named use; the City treats large-scale data centres as Major Industrial (permitted IH; IM only where existing 1 Jan 2024); Minor Industrial permitted in BE, IM, UI and IH-existing; Direct Control site-specific; s. 7.20(3.3.2) may make an ill-fitting use discretionary
quantities.status: sourced for standard zones; Edmonton Major or Minor turns on the data centre's own effects (Development Planner decides)

quantities.name: What a rezoning takes
quantities.formula: duration + application fee + levies and charges on new floor area
quantities.coef: Vancouver: target ~15 months to decision (~1 year from fee to hearing); CD-1 fee $94,500 (elsewhere) or $226,300 (downtown/Broadway) + $1,590 per 100 m² under 8,000 m²; DCL industrial $112.87/m², mixed employment $211.54/m² (none if floor area does not increase); ACC $12.92–24.22/m² from 30 Sep 2026; CAC exempt for 100 % industrial after 30 Sep 2026. Also where the City attaches conditions (111 E 5th heat delivery) and residents get a say (579 submissions). Edmonton (2026 Planning and Development Fee Schedules, effective 1 Jan 2026): rezoning to an Industrial zone (BE, IM, IH, … DC/IND) $2,745 base + $340/ha; Direct Control — Administrative $7,930, Minor $7,930 + $0.62/m² buildable, Major $15,855 + $1.06/m² buildable (Major = significant change in character or intensity, comprehensive site planning with technical studies); plus a notification and engagement fee of $1,650 per component; development permit, non-residential new building $1,220 + $500 lot-grading inspection up to 500 m² GFA, + $1.20/m² above; building permit $11 per $1,000 construction value to $1 M, $10 per $1,000 above. Off-site levies (Facilities Bylaw 19340, consolidated 23 Apr 2024; Arterial Roads Bylaw 14380, consolidated May 2026) are charged as a condition of subdivision (and, for arterial roads, development permit) only within defined catchments, mostly new neighbourhoods and industrial areas; rates are set in a separate annual document (2026 Off-site Levies Approved Rates, not yet retrieved). Edmonton rezoning duration still not stated; Edmonton duration: rezoning target 160 calendar days (~5.5 months) for complex files, which include all Direct Control zones, if a pre-application meeting is held; 90 days for non-complex; very complex set at the pre-application meeting (Rezoning Application Complexity, 1 Jan 2024); actual April–June 2026: 147-day average, 70% within target (Processing Times page); then public hearing, typically every two weeks. Fire hall off-site levy (Bylaw 19340) 2026 rates per hectare at subdivision, held at 2024–25 levels: e.g. Mistatim Industrial $23,724, EETP $20,618, Northeast EETP $12,816, Blatchford $32,813 (range $12,816–42,032)
quantities.status: Vancouver and Edmonton fees and durations in hand; Edmonton arterial-road assessment rates not retrieved

quantities.name: Consultation and rights that apply
quantities.formula: list the approvals an option needs that trigger consultation; describe, never predict
quantities.coef: Alberta: Water Act licences, public-land dispositions and environmental approvals wait on consultation; EPEA approval for backup generation over 50 MW. BC: Water Sustainability Act licences, BCUC CPCNs, City of Vancouver UNDRIP Strategy — to source. BC Hydro's 2026 Call for Demand scores First Nations criteria at 10 %. The tool never speaks for the Nations
quantities.status: Alberta partly in hand; BC to source

quantities.name: People within reach
quantities.formula: dissemination-area population × share of the DA within each radius (noise, light, heat receivers)
quantities.coef: 2021 census counts by dissemination area, spread evenly within each area onto a 100 m grid and summed within 200 m, 500 m and the sound distance: people, households, 65+, under 15, renter households, households spending 30%+ on shelter, people in low income (LIM-AT % × population). Randomly rounded; suppressed values count as 0

quantities.name: Work created
quantities.formula: floor area ÷ 5,000 ft² per operating job; construction peak separately
quantities.coef: Virginia JLARC 2024: about one full-time worker per 5,000 sq ft, about half contract; ~1,500 at peak construction for large campuses — transferred from Virginia hyperscale, use with caution at urban scale

quantities.name: Time to build and connect
quantities.formula: planning and permits + construction + grid connection (often the longest)
quantities.coef: 12–18 months per building; 2–3 years to operation; grid can add 12–36 months (JLARC; IEA); Vancouver rezoning ~15 months; Edmonton permit data give build times for non-residential permits since 2024; Edmonton permit processing (targets / actual average April–June 2026): development permit, commercial or industrial new building 90 days / 73 days (76% within target); building permit, commercial/industrial 120 days / 64 days (86%); excludes notification and appeal periods
quantities.status: in hand (transferred); local derivation possible for Edmonton

quantities.name: Reclaimed water as cooling make-up
quantities.formula: V_rec = s × make-up, with make-up = evaporation × C ÷ (C − 1)
quantities.coef: C (cycles of concentration) 2–4 typical, up to 6 (FEMP/EPA); 4–6 run on treated municipal wastewater (US DOE-funded study, 2012; power-plant scale); s = share substituted, user-set 0–1; operator precedents 0.74–0.99 (Microsoft, operator claim); data-centre site water 0.32–0.36 L/kWh (LBNL 2024, denominator to confirm); Metro Vancouver will consider supplying reclaimed water case by case for industrial uses (UT-019, 2023); EPCOR Gold Bar already supplies treated water to industry (operator claim, no volumes); no Canadian data-centre case found
quantities.status: screening; Vancouver and Edmonton supply volumes and prices not found

quantities.name: Greywater available from neighbours
quantities.formula: V_gw = residents within reach × 98 L/person/day × 365; used = min(V_gw × recovery, make-up)
quantities.coef: 98 L/person/day residential greywater (National Academies 2016, US data); treatment recovery share not found (gap); cross-property sharing: no BC or Alberta rule text found

quantities.name: Electricity to treat reused water
quantities.formula: E = m³ treated × e
quantities.coef: e = 0.75–1.1 kWh/m³ greywater membrane bioreactor; 0.94–1.28 mixed wastewater (Arden et al. 2021, US EPA authors); ~4.6 kWh/m³ in one small blackwater plant (university report, low confidence); viable only where water + sewer cost ≥ US$2.38/m³ (greywater) or US$1.85/m³ (mixed) (Arden 2021, US 2020 dollars)

quantities.name: Blowdown recovered
quantities.formula: make-up × 0.84; blowdown × 0.47; + 3,541 kWh/yr per skid
quantities.coef: one US federal test (GSA GPG-052, NREL evaluation, 2023): blowdown −53 %, make-up −16 %, cycles 2.8 → 4.9; US$46.8k installed; hard water, single site

quantities.name: Solar on the data centre roof
quantities.formula: kWp = roof area × 0.66 × (1 − plant share) × 0.70 × 0.16–0.20; MWh = kWp × yield
quantities.coef: yield, annual kWh/kWp (NRCan municipal values, ±10%, losses in a 0.75 performance ratio): Vancouver 892 horizontal to 1007 at latitude tilt; Edmonton 944 to 1244. A flat-roof array at about 15° tilt lies between the two, so the tool uses horizontal as the low end and latitude tilt as the high end. Edmonton yields about 6–24% more than Vancouver per kWp. Module density 0.16 kWp/m² (2014 median) to 0.20 (current) (NREL); module cover 0.70 of a flat roof at 15° tilt; 66% of large roofs suitable (NREL 2016); roof share taken by plant from the cooling module

quantities.name: Solar on the facade
quantities.formula: MWh = south facade area × module density × vertical yield
quantities.coef: vertical (south-facing, 90°) yield, annual kWh/kWp: Vancouver 716, Edmonton 989 (NRCan municipal values). Vertical gives 71% of the latitude-tilt yield in Vancouver and 80% in Edmonton; in Edmonton a south wall yields more than a flat roof (989 vs 944), because of low winter sun. Replaces the interim 0.4–0.6 factor. No Canadian BIPV cost found

quantities.name: Battery storage
quantities.formula: MWh = MW × hours (1–8, default 4); area m² = kWh ÷ 34 (19–49)
quantities.coef: round-trip 85% (NREL ATB 2024); PNNL 2022 LFP, 2021 US$ installed: 1 MW 518.59/kWh (2 h) and 448.34 (4 h), 10 MW 461.15 and 410.70 — about 10% above the 100 MW figure of 385; 2030: 340.46 (1 MW 4 h), 311.11 (10 MW 4 h); RTE 83% at the transformer, 2,400 cycles at 80% DOD, 16-year life; 34 ± 15 kWh/m² across built sites (Reber 2023); fire-code basis in BC/AB (NFPA 855 adoption) unconfirmed

quantities.formula: flexible MWh = IT load × UPS minutes ÷ 60 × 0.5 (half held for outages)
quantities.coef: UPS runtime 1–2 min (hyperscale), ~5 min (colocation), 10–15 min (financial) — vendor figures, operator claim; useful for fast frequency response, not for 4-hour peaks

quantities.coef: testing ≈14.5 h/yr per unit, ~4 h at full load (AUC 27938-D01-2023, Amazon 25.6 MW, derived); Vancouver noise by-law exemption caps tests ≈15 h/yr; uncontrolled diesel 14.6 g NOx, 0.43 g PM, 706 g CO2 per kWh (AP-42 Table 3.4-1, upper bound for modern engines); Alberta exempts standby generators from environmental approval

quantities.coef: BC approved fuel codes −7 to 131 g CO2e/MJ (RLCF-012, Apr 2026); stack CO2, NOx and PM stay about the same; fossil diesel reference CI to retrieve

quantities.name: Borefield as the data centre's heat sink
quantities.formula: L = heat to ground (W) ÷ q; boreholes = L ÷ 150 m; area = boreholes × 36 m²
quantities.coef: q = 12 W/m ground-only to 19 W/m with a dry cooler (derived from Zurmuhl et al. 2018, a 14.5 kW data centre, Ithaca, k 3.27 W/m·K); Edmonton design k 1.9 W/m·K (Alberta Geological Survey) → ~7–11 W/m (scaling is an assumption); ≈2 ha of borefield per MW rejected; 40 MW ≈ 0.8 km²; screening only — CSA C448 sizing and a thermal response test required; no Vancouver ground data found

quantities.name: Ground warming over 20 years
quantities.formula: from the share of heat put in vs taken out
quantities.coef: +4.7 K over 20 yr ground-only, +1.2 K with a dry cooler (Zurmuhl 2018, small field); about +3 K in 3 yr where 4.8 × more heat went in than out (Kindaichi 2018, field measurement) — a borefield only lasts if neighbours take heat back out in winter

quantities.name: Seasonal ground store for neighbours
quantities.formula: heat out = η × heat stored; boreholes = charge W ÷ 47–83 W/m ÷ 35–55 m
quantities.coef: η 0.45 steady state (simulated), 0.32–0.56 measured years 3–10, 0.06–0.21 in years 1–2 (Drake Landing, Okotoks); a 0.9 MW data-centre design: 240 boreholes, 55 m deep, 3 m apart, 1,863 m², waste-heat use 77 → 96 %, ~17-yr payback (Li et al. 2021); heat-pump COP for the lift not given (gap)

quantities.name: Aquifer heat store (open loop)
quantities.formula: flow = MW × 3.6 ÷ (4.18 × ΔT); heat out ≈ 0.6 × heat in
quantities.coef: 172 m³/h per MW at ΔT 5 K (assumption); injection ≤25 °C typical (Netherlands limit; no BC/AB limit found) — air-cooled data-centre heat (25–35 °C) may exceed it; recovery 0.6 (0.4–0.85), ≈ €300/kW at 2 MW (Barth et al. 2026); BC: water licence (WSA); Alberta: Water Act approval or licence + professional report

quantities.name: Deep geothermal heat
quantities.formula: MWth = flow × c × (T_res − T_return)
quantities.coef: Edmonton: ~90 °C at 2.5 km, 30–80 kg/s → 2.1–5.6 MWth average per well pair, $4.7–8 M per well (Majorowicz & Grasby 2021); licensed by the AER (Directive 089, 2025); competes with data-centre heat as a district source rather than cooling the data centre; Vancouver: not plausible for power, direct use unproven

quantities.name: Hot or chilled water tank
quantities.formula: litres per kWh = 3,600 ÷ (4.18 × ΔT) ÷ 0.85
quantities.coef: 144 L/kWh at ΔT 6 K, 29 L/kWh at 30 K (physics); ice ≈ 10.5 kg per kWh; usable share 0.85 and tank heights are assumptions; costs too wide to use (IRENA range)

quantities.name: Cooling for neighbours from waste heat
quantities.formula: cooling = recovered heat × COP, if temperature allows
quantities.coef: single-effect absorption needs ≥90 °C, COP 0.6–0.7; two-stage 70–80 °C, COP <0.4 (Energies 2026); data-centre heat 25–35 °C air-cooled (no), 50–60 °C liquid-cooled (only with a heat-pump lift)

quantities.name: Buildable envelope
quantities.formula: max floor area = site area × FSR (or FAR) available to the data-centre use; height, setbacks and building-width limits from the zone
quantities.coef: Vancouver I-3 A: FSR 3.00 (bonus not open to storage uses), 18.3 m (30.5 m discretionary), side yard 7.6 m, max building width and depth 61.0 m, floor-to-floor ≥ 6.0 m ground / 4.0 m above; FC-2: FSR 1.00–5.00 by sub-area (6.50 at discretion), 10.7–22.9 m (to 51.8 m), side yards not permitted; I-2: FSR 3.00, 18.3 m (to 30.5–36.5 m); I-1C: FSR 6.00, 46.5 m. Vancouver counts plant floor space above grade (excluded only at or below base surface, e.g. I-2 s. 4.1.2(c)). Edmonton IM: 18.0 m, FAR 2.0, setbacks 3.0 m street / 6.0 m to non-industrial; IH: 30.0 m, FAR 2.0, min site 1.0 ha; BE: 16.0 m, FAR 1.6. Edmonton s. 5.70(1.9): ventilating equipment, mechanical penthouses, tanks and stacks have no height limit

quantities.name: Space for the plant
quantities.formula: Σ components (electrical yard and switchgear, UPS and batteries, generators and fuel, heat rejection, heat recovery, fire suppression, loading) × IT load × redundancy
quantities.coef: Manufacturer claims per MW: UPS ≈2.0–2.4 m², Li-ion batteries ≈2.2 m² (5 min), air-cooled chillers 17–26 m², cooling towers ≈8 m², dry coolers ≈24.5 m², heat pumps ≈3.4 m² per MW heat, CDUs ≈0.6 m²; equipment only, without clearances; EPCOR transformer clearances 3.0 m door side / 2.0 m others; fuel room 2 h separation and 550 mm clearance (NFC 4.3.14); generator room 2 h (VBBL 3.6.2.8)

quantities.name: Room for the data hall
quantities.formula: new: envelope floor area − plant space − support − ground-floor uses the zone requires; part of an existing building: the floor area offered
quantities.coef: Vancouver I-2, I-3 and FC-2: no data storage at the ground floor except entrances; calibration: Burlington 3,710 m² of halls = 48–72 % of gross area
quantities.status: arithmetic on sourced limits; white-space share from one calibration case

quantities.name: Largest size that fits
quantities.formula: hall area ÷ area per MW (range); for part of a building, also capped by floor load, electrical service and heat-rejection space
quantities.coef: LBNL prototypes 3.7–13.9 m² per rack → ≈186–2,325 m² per MW; Ark UP4 28 MW IT in 15,410 m² (three buildings); 111 E 5th ≤ 291 m² per MW (upper bound); Uptime 2024 average 8 kW per rack (industry survey)
quantities.status: range, wide; narrows with rack density

quantities.name: Floor strength
quantities.formula: equipment load of the hall (racks, batteries) vs the floor's design load for its original use
quantities.coef: NBC 2020 Table 4.1.5.3: office 2.4 kPa (upper floors), 4.8 kPa (basement and ground floors with exterior access); equipment and service rooms ≥ 3.6 kPa; office row excludes computer rooms; data halls designed for actual loads (4.1.5.1.(1)); data-hall values 7.2 kPa (US DoD) and 12 kPa (TIA-942 Rated-3) need the standard
quantities.status: code values sourced; data-hall loads need the standard

quantities.name: Fuel kept on site
quantities.formula: generator capacity × runtime hours × fuel per kWh, against the limit per storage room for the storey it sits on
quantities.coef: NFC 2020 Table 4.3.13.4.-B (Class II): first storey 200 000 L per room; basement or above the first storey 20 000 L (tanks > 2 500 L) or 45 000 L (tanks > 20 000 L); tanks > 230 L in a dedicated 2 h room; fuel use ≈0.263 L/kWh (one Cat model, manufacturer claim) ≈6.3 m³ per MW per 24 h; Uptime ≥ 12 h on site; whether data-centre standby counts as "emergency generators" is for the authority to decide
quantities.status: code limits sourced; fuel rate is a manufacturer claim

quantities.name: Flood exposure
quantities.unit: m above or below the flood level
quantities.formula: floor elevation of the plant vs the flood construction level, for parcels in the designated floodplain
quantities.coef: Vancouver FCL 4.6 m (GVRD datum, includes 1 m sea-level rise to 2100, 1:500-yr, 0.6 m freeboard); switchgear, electrical panels and fire protection not below FCL unless flood-protected (VBBL Div. C 2.2.9.3(2)); main switchgear in industrial buildings at or above FCL (F014 s. 3.3)
quantities.status: Vancouver sourced; datum conversion not found; Edmonton not yet looked at

quantities.name: Vibration to neighbours
quantities.unit: ranked: slab on grade → long-span upper floor
quantities.formula: qualitative rank of how hard plant vibration is to isolate at each position in the building
quantities.coef: NBC/VBBL apparent STC 47 between dwellings and other spaces (STC 55 by elevator shafts) — airborne only, no equipment-vibration limit; isolator deflection rises with floor span (US government spec citing ASHRAE); ASHRAE Applications ch. 49 not read

quantities.name: Electrical service
quantities.formula: IT load × PUE → the utility service class and what it brings (second feeder, transmission, clearances)
quantities.coef: BC Hydro: above 6.5 MVA (12.5 kV areas) or 13 MVA (25 kV areas) a two-feeder supply may be required; 60 kV and above under transmission rules. EPCOR: primary service typical above 2,500 kVA; transformer clearances 3.0 m / 2.0 m; access road 4.6 m in a 6.5 m strip

quantities.name: Receivers within reach
quantities.unit: list: type, distance, demand, temperature, evidence
quantities.formula: every candidate receiver whose straight-line distance ≤ its type's reach (receiver_radius); each carries its demand (disclosed, else floor area × intensity), the temperature its type needs, its profile, and where the record came from
quantities.coef: types: hot-water district network · ambient (low-temperature) network · steam network · pool · ice rink (also a source) · school · hospital or care home · housing · office · greenhouse · wastewater plant. Pools: water ≤ 37 °C by regulation, 25–28 °C recommended for competition pools (BC 2025). Ambient networks (Blatchford) take heat near ground temperature and lift it in each building. Hot water stored for taps must be at least 60 °C, and 49 °C anywhere in a recirculation loop (Vancouver Building By-law 2025 Book II, 2.6.1.12.(1), 2.6.1.1.(3)); so data-centre heat at 25–35 °C can preheat tap water but a heat pump or other source must finish it. Map records (15 Oct 2026, tool/receivers_*.json): Vancouver 353 — 27 recreation centres, 1 arena, 20 hospitals, 103 care homes, 202 schools (StatCan ODSRF v2 records no separate Vancouver pools; recreation-centre contents not recorded) — plus 641 non-market housing projects (City open data); Edmonton 475 — 161 recreation centres, 23 pools, 22 indoor arenas, 13 hospitals, 2 care homes, 254 schools. 72 health records have no location and are counted, not placed. Arena ice plants are heat sources as well as receivers.
quantities.status: data in hand (15 Oct); Vancouver pools and Edmonton care homes thin in the national records

quantities.name: Other sources for the same receiver
quantities.formula: sources already serving, or planned for, each receiver: sewage heat recovery, wastewater plants, ice-rink refrigeration, other data centres, ground loops; a receiver whose demand is already met by a low-carbon source is a weaker match, not a missing one
quantities.coef: Vancouver NEU: 70% renewable, mostly sewage heat recovery, 6.6 MW added, 100% renewable target 2030 (City page, May 2025); Blatchford (Edmonton): ambient loop on geo-exchange and sewer heat. Ice rinks reject refrigeration heat — a source as well as a receiver. NEU By-law 9552 (2026): inside its service area, new buildings and major alterations must take NEU heat unless the City Engineer finds it not practical or economical (s. 2.1); heat returned to the network is credited at 50% of $65.172/MWh. Traced service area (2.3 km², ±45 m): 111 E 5th Ave lies inside, 70–130 m from the line — consistent with RTS 19744 making NEU heat delivery a material condition of that data centre

quantities.status: two networks sourced; others per receiver

quantities.name: What the receiver uses now
quantities.formula: the heat source a match would replace: from the host-building question (gas boilers · hot-water system · electric baseboard · district energy) or the network's supply mix; carbon change = displaced heat × its factor − heat-pump electricity × grid factor, which can be zero or negative where the displaced source is already low-carbon
quantities.coef: factors from grid_co2 (NIR 2026) and the network's own reported mix; a network share described as "renewable" is the operator's word and is shown as such
quantities.status: logic defined; factors per network to source

quantities.name: Hour-by-hour match
quantities.unit: % of receiver demand met · MWh surplus · MW backup
quantities.formula: for each hour of the typical year: delivered = min(heat available, receiver demand); report the share of the receiver's annual demand met, the heat still rejected (surplus), and the receiver's peak that must be met without the data centre
quantities.coef: annual totals overstate the match: Vancouver heat demand is 47% in Dec–Feb and 2.5% in Jun–Aug (CWEC, computed); the data centre's heat is near-flat

quantities.name: Who controls the computing
quantities.formula: flexible load is offered only by whoever runs the workloads: a single-owner or hyperscale operator can shift its own computing; in colocation the building operator controls power and cooling, not the tenants' computing, so flexibility needs each tenant's agreement
quantities.coef: business model from operator pages (claims) and permits; the learning-series EV and workload papers are models of single-operator fleets
quantities.status: logic defined; per-site model from operator pages; Crozier & Liska 2025: no published flexible share — inference is inflexible, checkpointed training can pause

quantities.name: How firm the exchange is
quantities.formula: existing = operating; committed = in a contract, permit condition or funded budget; planned = in a utility filing or adopted plan; proposed = an applicant or operator says so; possible = the tool found it and nobody has proposed it. Only existing and committed count as delivered
quantities.coef: states and rule set 14 Oct 2026 (learning-series critique); promised heat that is only possible is shown, never counted

quantities.name: Futures
quantities.formula: rerun the match in four futures: (1) as planned; (2) the tenant changes cooling — air ↔ liquid changes heat temperature, capture share and flexibility; (3) the tenant leaves — the receiver's backup carries its full peak and the building's reusable parts are listed; (4) the receiver leaves — all heat goes back to rejection, so full rejection capacity stays
quantities.coef: lifespans from horizons (servers ~6 years, plant 15–25, network 40–50); closure cases in meta.lifecycle

conditions.test: competing_sources for the receiver: none, spare demand left, or already met by a low-carbon source
conditions.note: Near the NEU the data centre competes with sewage heat recovery; the match may still work for the share the sewer cannot cover.
conditions.next_action: ask the network operator what it already plans to supply

conditions.heading: 3 Temporal
conditions.name: Supply meets demand hour by hour
conditions.test: hourly_overlap: share of the receiver's demand met, surplus rejected, backup peak named
conditions.next_action: the receiver's monthly bills or meter data; otherwise the tool uses the typical-year profile and says so

conditions.heading: 3 Temporal
conditions.name: Still works if the receiver leaves
conditions.test: futures (4): full heat rejection kept on site; nothing in the data centre depends on the receiver
conditions.next_action: hourly or monthly demand data from the receiver

conditions.heading: 3 Temporal
conditions.name: Still works if the tenant changes
conditions.test: futures (2) and (3): the receiver's backup carries its peak; the interface takes a different heat temperature
conditions.next_action: hourly or monthly demand data from the receiver

conditions.heading: 5 Organizational
conditions.name: Whoever runs the computing agrees to shift it
conditions.test: workload_control: operator, or tenants who have opted in
conditions.next_action: the operator's business model (single owner, hyperscale, colocation)

conditions.heading: 5 Organizational
conditions.name: The exchange is committed, not only possible
conditions.test: commitment is existing or committed; otherwise shown as a possibility with what would commit it
conditions.note: Guards against a heat promise that wins approval and is never built (see Promises enforceable).
conditions.next_action: a contract, permit condition or budget line

conditions.heading: 6 Regulatory
conditions.name: Inside a compulsory district-energy area
conditions.test: parcel inside a service area where new buildings must connect (Vancouver NEU, By-law 9552 s. 2.1): the data centre becomes a customer; heat sent back is credited at half the energy charge
conditions.note: Section 5.2(a)(v) allows equipment that recovers waste heat from a building's cooling system. The 50% credit ($32.59/MWh) is the City's posted price for returned heat — one end of the price window.
conditions.next_action: check the parcel against Schedule A; ask the City Engineer whether service is required
